task: What settlements has Wells Fargo reached?

merged.claim: In October 2026 (announced Oct 15), state securities regulators announced a combined $4.4 million multistate settlement with Wells Fargo (Clearing Services, Advisors Financial Network) and Merrill Lynch over excessive/unreasonable commissions.

c1.note: NASAA Oct 15, 2026 release confirms combined $4.4M settlement with the Wells Fargo entities and Merrill Lynch.

c4.note: More than 256,000 transactions combined; Wells Fargo accounts for about 228,243 (228,243 + 28,162 = 256,405).

c6.note: Nearly $3.9M in excess commissions with restitution plus 6% interest.

c7.note: Merrill's excess commissions were nearly $549,000, which concerns Merrill rather than Wells Fargo.

c11.note: Montana calls it an agreement in principle; the no-admit/no-deny wording is standard for these consent orders but is not quoted in the passages.

c12.note: The settlement website confirms the $85M cash settlement over Diverse Search statements, with the named defendants.

c13.note: The settlement site states final approval was granted on May 21, 2026.

c14.note: The judgment file is named as signed 9/11/2026 by Judge Thompson, though its text did not extract.

c15.note: The site states defendants deny all allegations and any liability.

c16.note: The $85M is the cash settlement fund, and the fee and expense deductions come out of it; the sources don't spell this out for this case, so this rests on standard class-settlement structure.

c17.note: The class period of Feb 24, 2021 to June 9, 2022 is confirmed.

c18.note: The $110M derivative settlement over hiring and lending discrimination is confirmed, with final approval by Judge Thompson.

c19.note: The May 15, 2026 release announces final approval; the exact order date may be slightly earlier.

c20.note: Approval was announced May 15, so May 18 is only the date of the BFA post, not the grant date.

c21.note: The $100M Borrower Assistance Fund is confirmed.

c22.note: The $10M paid to Wells Fargo by directors' insurers is confirmed.

c23.note: The $50M J&J Ponzi settlement in D. Nev. is confirmed, including the IOLTA-based claims.

c24.note: Preliminary approval on July 9, 2026 is confirmed.

c25.note: The final approval hearing is set for Nov 12, 2026, the day after the run date, so approval is still pending.

c27.note: The $56.85M California CARES Act credit-reporting class settlement is confirmed.

c28.note: The settlement website says the court approved the settlement on June 10, 2026.

c29.note: Wells Fargo denies wrongdoing or liability and settled to avoid litigation cost and uncertainty.

c9.note: A search snippet of the Massachusetts order E-2026-2136 (Oct 15, 2026) shows a $38,000 administrative fine payable to the Commonwealth. I could not read the PDF text myself.

c10.note: The order cites $79,761.45 in over-5% commissions on 1,631 Massachusetts residents, with restitution plus 6% interest, and the firms neither admit nor deny. I could not confirm the censure from the text I could access.

c26.note: The page says Wells Fargo denies any wrongdoing or knowledge of the scheme.

c51.note: The settlement site states the third distribution occurred on September 18, 2026. This is a payout detail of the 2023 $1B settlement, not a new settlement.
